parts.text: In this experiment, you will determine the density of water. Carry out the following instructions, referring to Fig. 1.1. You are provided with a plastic drinks cup.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (a) (i) Place the cup, with the base at the bottom, in square A on this page. Draw carefully around the base of the cup. Remove the cup from the paper. Take measurements from your drawing to determine an accurate value for the diameter D B of the base of the cup. Square A D B = .................................................... cm [2]

ms.label: 1(a)(i)
ms.text:
2 or more measurements
D correct within ± 2 mm
B

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Place the cup, with the rim at the bottom, in square B on this page. Draw carefully around the rim of the cup. Remove the cup from the paper. Take measurements from your drawing to determine the diameter D T of the rim of the cup. Square B D T = .................................................... cm [1]

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Calculate the average diameter D of the cup using the equation D = D B + D T 2 . D = .................................................... cm [1]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) You are provided with water in beaker W . Pour a volume V / 2 of water into the measuring cylinder. Pour this water into the cup.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Use the balance provided to measure the mass m of the cup containing the water. m = ....................................................... g [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Determine the density ρ of water using the equation ρ = 2 m V . Give your answer to a suitable number of significant figures for this experiment. Include the unit. ρ = .......................................................... [3]
